# Paired-device discovery vectors

This revision is intended for `paired-devices-vectors-v1.5`; the published
`paired-devices-vectors-v1.4` tag remains unchanged.

`cases.json` is generated by the production `callosum.paired_devices_read` and
`callosum.paired_devices_watch` handlers. Requests require empty object params, and the daemon must
identify the caller as `reserved:claustrum`; any other caller is refused. Successful replies contain
`devices` (sorted by fingerprint) and `self.static_public_key_hex`; the operation
refuses if the serving identity is unavailable. See `docs/push-wire.md` for device
eligibility and the opaque, equality-only `pairing_id` contract.
Each device includes `shares`, sorted by share id, with only the caller module's
live switches for that device's current class. Disabled switches are included;
`enabled` requires a non-empty effective grant. Watch cases record the initial
full snapshot in `notices`; refusals arrive before any notice. Later snapshots
have the same shape and are coalesced to at most one per second.

A case's `caller`, when present, overrides the top-level caller.
`occipital_caller` pins that `reserved:occipital` is refused.

The fixture's serving X25519 Noise static public key is:

```text
8520f0098930a754748b7ddcb43ef75a0dbf3a0d26381af4eba4a98eaa9b4e6a
```

Its fingerprint is `300c9c9603b92a4b39ed3958bf924011`. Decode the 64 lowercase
hex characters to 32 bytes, hash those bytes with SHA-256, take the first 16
bytes of the digest, then encode them as 32 lowercase hex characters. Do not
hash the hex text. The corresponding typed identity is
`fed-computer:300c9c9603b92a4b39ed3958bf924011`; the vault can derive that
fingerprint from `self.static_public_key_hex` to check its typed computer.
This is a public test fixture, not a production identity.

Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
UPDATE_PAIRED_DEVICES_VECTORS=1 cargo test --locked -p fed-module --lib paired_devices_read::tests::vectors_match_production -- --exact --nocapture
```

Run the same command without the environment variable to check for drift.
On a read-only build checkout, set `PAIRED_DEVICES_VECTOR_OUTPUT_DIR` to an
untracked output directory; the test writes `cases.json` and `SHA256SUMS` there.
The path is relative to `crates/fed-module`, the test's working directory. Copy
the generated files back to `test-vectors/paired-devices/` after the test exits.
Regeneration writes `SHA256SUMS` for this README and `cases.json`.
After regeneration, update the SHA-256 pin for `cases.json` in
`test-vectors/scan-vendored-ids.py`.
